title: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)

sections.label: Fathers' leave timing
sections.summary: Asks whether the Minister will consider letting fathers take leave at any stage within weeks of their baby's birth, not just within the first 16 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Within the recognition of the importance of supporting working mums, will the Minister consider allowing fathers to take leave at any stage within weeks of their baby's birth and not just within the first 16 weeks?

sections.label: Early childhood manpower plans
sections.summary: Asks about the Ministry's contingency plan if early childhood manpower falls short, and whether it will consider retired teachers or flexi-work measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In his parliamentary reply earlier this year, the Minister shared that a projected number of 1,500 more early childhood personnel over the next two to three years is needed to meet the demand.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Second, what is the Ministry's contingency plan if the manpower supply still falls short in two to three years' time, bearing in mind that we are near full employment and there is a manpower shortage across all sectors?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: And, lastly, would the Ministry consider complementary measures, such as drawing in retired teachers, not necessarily retired preschool teachers, or "aunties" who do not have the papers but are experienced enough to help at the centres, as an interim supply-side solution; or work with the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) to promote flexi-work that will, as part of the demand-side solution, enable mothers, fathers and grandparents to have more time to care for their children?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The 390 childcare centres at workplaces were also well spread out.

sections.label: KiFAS and childcare subsidies
sections.summary: Calls for KiFAS expansion to all kindergartens and asks whether the basic subsidy for middle-income parents will be increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Page: 81 Madam, I am repeating my earlier calls for KiFAS to be expanded to all kindergartens so as to create more quality choices of learning and development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This will impact 169 childcare centres and help 16,500 children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: To defray child-raising costs, all Singapore citizen children enrolled in centre-based care are eligible for a basic subsidy of up to $300 for childcare per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In April 2013, additional subsidies were introduced to help families with gross household income of $7,500 or per capita income of $1,875.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: From 2011 to 2015, the median full-day fees rose 25%, yet the subsidies for those families in the sandwiched group, which is those above the 40th percentile, remained unchanged at $300 since 2008.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry increase the amount of basic subsidy given to these middle-income parents?

sections.label: Single mums' mental health
sections.summary: A 2007 study found single mums are significantly more likely to have moderate to severe mental disability, citing income, hardship and social support reasons.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2007 study by Crozier, Butterworth and Rogers found that single mums are significantly more likely to have a moderate to severe mental disability.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, the study shows that prevalence of mental health issues in single mums is almost 30%, compared to partnered mothers, which is about 15%.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The study cites decreased household income, increased financial hardship and a perceived lack of social support as the main reasons for single mums to have an increased risk of poor mental health.

sections.label: CPF top-ups for caregivers
sections.summary: Hopes the Government will look into CPF top-ups for full-time informal caregivers in low-income households facing under-employment and retirement pressure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In recent years, we are starting to acknowledge and provide assistance to these informal caregivers, with several Members of this House having spoken on the issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will look into CPF top-ups for full-time informal caregivers in low-income households to reduce the pressure of being under-employed and under-prepared for retirement, as a result of taking on their informal caregiving responsibilities.

sections.label: SSOs helping families
sections.summary: Suggests MSF's SSOs pick out such families and provide a holistic approach with more lasting solutions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Maybe MSF's SSOs can pick out such families and provide a holistic approach in helping them with more lasting solutions.

sections.label: Spousal loss and mixed marriages
sections.summary: It states that losing a spouse is a huge struggle and that marriages between Singaporeans and non-Singaporeans are increasing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is a huge struggle that they have to grapple with when their spouse passes away.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: There are increasingly more marriages between Singaporeans and non-Singaporeans.

sections.label: Chinese national's stateless triplets
sections.summary: Media reported on a Chinese national whose Singaporean husband left; her previously stateless triplets were recently granted citizenship with a lawyer's aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Recently, several media reported on the plight of a Chinese national who gave birth to triplets after her Singaporean husband reportedly walked out of their marriage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Her children, who were previously stateless, were granted citizenship recently, with the aid of a helpful lawyer.

sections.label: Maternity leave for unmarried parents
sections.summary: It calls for equal support to all families and asks the Minister to consider extending Government Paid Maternity Leave to children of unmarried parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: We should offer the same level of support to families of all kinds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Hence, I would like the Minister to consider extending Government Paid Maternity Leave (GPML) to children of unmarried parents.

sections.label: Benefits excluded for unwed parents
sections.summary: It says Baby Bonus, housing priority schemes and family grants are not extended to unwed parents, and asks if the CDA First Step grant includes their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Whilst we have progressed and started in recent years to provide more for single parents, certain benefits, such as Baby Bonus and housing priority schemes and grants for families, are not extended to unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: I note the Finance Minister's earlier announcement that the Child Development Account (CDA)'s First Step grant is for all Singaporean children and I share the concerns of many other Members who have also asked if this will also include children of unwed parents.

sections.label: Let child benefit from CDA
sections.summary: It states that the child should be allowed to benefit from the Child Development Account.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Thirdly, allow the child to benefit from the CDA.

sections.label: First Step Grant and KidSTART
sections.summary: It states the child should enjoy the $3,000 First Step Grant and that children of divorced or unwed parents be included in KidSTART.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Second, it allows the child to also enjoy the First Step Grant of $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Lastly, ensure that children of divorced or unwed parents are included in the KidSTART programme.

sections.label: Children born out of wedlock
sections.summary: Children born out of wedlock are not entitled to this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Children born out of wedlock are not entitled to this.

sections.label: Single parent HDB eligibility
sections.summary: A single parent below 35 and their child do not form a family nucleus for new HDB or rental flat applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A single parent below the age of 35 and their child do not form a family nucleus when applying for a new HDB flat or rental flat.

sections.label: Unwed mothers maternity leave
sections.summary: Unwed mothers are not covered under the Child Development Co-Savings Act, so employers pay eight weeks and four weeks depend on employment terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Page: 87 First, their mothers are not covered under the Child Development Co-Savings Act which entitles lawfully-wedded mothers to 16 weeks of maternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: For the single unwed mothers, employers pay them for the first eight weeks, with the next four weeks subjected to employment terms.

sections.label: Children without CDA benefits
sections.summary: Children without a CDA cannot enjoy benefits like the $3,000 CDA First Step Grant; in 2014 there were 446 children born without the father's name.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: Second, because these children do not have a CDA, they would not be able to enjoy benefits, such as the CDA First Step Grant of $3,000 which would have been very handy for the financially-strained single mothers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: In 2014, there were 446 children born without the father's name.

sections.label: Abuse cases in 2014
sections.summary: In 2014 there were 158 cases with clear evidence of abuse and 47 cases lacking evidence but needing assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: In 2014, there were 158 cases where there was clear evidence of abuse, with another 47 cases lacking evidence but needing assistance.

sections.label: ComCare assistance recipients increase
sections.summary: ComCare Short-To-Medium-Term Assistance recipients rose from over 11,000 in FY2012 to over 27,000 in FY2014, which the speaker attributes to expanded eligibility and greater outreach.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, the Ministry's ComCare Annual Report reported that the number of recipients of ComCare Short-To-Medium-Term Assistance increased from over 11,000 beneficiaries in Financial Year 2012 to over 27,000 beneficiaries in Financial Year 2014.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I believe this is due to the expansion of the eligibility for Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance in 2012 and 2014 and also the greater outreach effort by the SSOs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, all else being equal, the effectiveness of Government's efforts to help Singaporeans in need should be reflected in a decline of the number eligible for assistance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Recent studies show that asset and cash transfers to the poor are more effective when the recipients receive two years of counselling and training to use the assets and cash in ways that will help them to graduate from poverty.

sections.label: ComCare report graduation data
sections.summary: The ComCare Annual Report should show the number graduating from ComCare through the Mentoring Programme, not just beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The ComCare Annual Report should also show the number graduating from ComCare through the Mentoring Programme, not just the number of beneficiaries, so that we can be confident our fellow Singaporeans are being uplifted out of poverty.

sections.label: Past recidivism rate
sections.summary: The recidivism rate back then was high, at 44.4%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recidivism rate back then was high, at 44.4%.

sections.label: Recidivism drop and recognition
sections.summary: Recidivism dropped from 44.4% to the mid-20s from 2011, and the approach inspired prison systems elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recidivism rate has dropped from 44.4% to the mid-20s from 2011 onwards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Public perception of ex-offenders and morale of prison officers remain high and our innovative approach has actually gone on to inspire similar experiments in prison systems from Nigeria to Australia.

sections.label: Poverty relapse and culture questions
sections.summary: It asks how many relapsed into poverty two years on and whether broad-based culture interventions are being tried.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, do we know how many of our people relapsed into poverty two years on despite our interventions?

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, are we experimenting with any broad-based "Yellow Ribbon"-like culture intervention to meet our strategic goal of disrupting poverty?

sections.label: Silver Support Scheme assistance
sections.summary: The Silver Support Scheme gives additional assistance to lower-income elderly on top of other assistance they may be eligible for.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would typically refer them to SSO and, usually, some form of assistance is given to them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, heartened that one of the key initiatives rolled out in this year's Budget is the Silver Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Through this scheme, additional assistance will be given to the elderly Page: 91 from the lower income group, on top of any other forms of assistance that they may already be eligible for.

sections.label: SSO support and children
sections.summary: Some are uncomfortable seeking help from children, and SSO sometimes withholds assistance where children should support their parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Some are also uncomfortable about seeking help from their children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have seen cases where SSO will extend some support but there are also several cases where assistance is not given on account of the fact that there are children who should be able to support their parents.

sections.label: Social mobility study frequency
sections.summary: The speaker notes methodological limits in two studies and suggests committing to at least one social mobility study every 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And there are methodological limitations to both these studies, as both authors have acknowledged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I suggest that we commit to at least one social mobility study every 10 years to the best available global standards.

sections.label: Assistive Technology Fund beneficiaries
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to update whether Singapore is close to the forecasted 400 beneficiaries taking up the Assistive Technology Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: In this case, can the Minister update us if we are close to the forecasted 400 beneficiaries taking up the Assistive Technology Fund?

sections.label: Support for congenital and pre-existing conditions
sections.summary: MediShield Life covers congenital and pre-existing conditions, with universal base funding for Early Intervention and MOE support for Special Education schools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: MediShield Life which covers persons with congenital conditions and/or pre-existing conditions; universal base funding on top of means-tested fundings for Early Intervention, and the immense MOE support for Special Education schools.

sections.label: Third Enabling Masterplan underway
sections.summary: The third five-year Enabling Masterplan for Persons with Disabilities in Singapore is now underway.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The third five-year Enabling Masterplan for Persons with Disabilities in our country is now underway.

sections.label: UN Convention ratification and rights
sections.summary: Singapore signed and ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2012 and 2013, which views them as full and equal members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Singapore signed and ratified the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2012 and 2013 respectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Convention advocates the important view that Persons with Disabilities should not be simply objects of charity, medical treatment and social protection.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Convention sees them as full and equal members of society with rights to such important things as education, healthcare, housing, justice, mobility and safety.

sections.label: Eligibility criteria for disability schemes
sections.summary: Administrators and policy writers must dive deeper, as using only physical Activities of Daily Living for eligibility is old-school.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Administrators and policy writers must themselves dive deeper, too.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is old-school to only use a person's ability or inability to perform physical Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) as the eligibility criteria to schemes, such as the Foreign Worker Grants for the disabled.

sections.label: Rare disease and disability support needs
sections.summary: Children with rare diseases, adults with severe disabilities and parents needing legal help for adult children lacking mental capacity need assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Children with rare diseases whose medical costs can chalk up to $300,000 per year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Although MediShield Life, thankfully, does not exclude them, the needs are still high and this group needs help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Centres for adults with more severe disabilities, receiving only means-tested financial support and insufficient for long-term viability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Parents who are in urgent need of legal assistance as they are no longer able to make decisions for their adult children deemed as lacking mental capacity; decisions, such as on surgeries and housing – they need help.

sections.label: Open Door Programme funding claims
sections.summary: About 140 companies applied for Open Door Programme funds, with an average claim of $3,000 per company.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Ms Chia Yong Yong, you have two cuts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I understand that, to date, around 140 companies have applied for funds under the Open Door Programme (ODP) and the average claim per company was $3,000.

sections.label: Permanency planning training funding
sections.summary: Permanency planning can be included in customised care plans, and the Government is urged to fund structured training for social service professionals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Permanency planning can be taken into account in the beneficiary's current customised care plans to enable caregivers and VWOs to have regular conversations on how to review and update such permanency planning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I urge the Government to consider providing funding support for social service professionals to undergo structured training for the purposes of undertaking permanency planning.

sections.label: SkillsFuture awards for social service professionals
sections.summary: The Government is developing skilled social service professionals, and recipients of SkillsFuture Study Awards for the Social Service Sector get $5,000 each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: The Government is now trying to develop a larger pool of skilled social service professionals through agencies, such as ECDA and the Social Service Institute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: We announced recently that in addition to the SkillsFuture Credit, social service professionals will also be eligible for the SkillsFuture Study Awards for the Social Service Sector, providing each recipient with $5,000 for attending course-related training.

sections.label: Raising social service professional salaries
sections.summary: The passage asks whether salaries of social workers and other social service professionals can continue to be raised for parity with peers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: In particular, can we continue to raise the salaries of social workers and other social service professionals to give them greater parity with their peers in other professions?

sections.label: SSNet implementation progress and next phase
sections.summary: The passage asks about the progress of SSNet implementation and its next phase of development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: How has the progress of the implementation of SSNet been and what is the next phase of its development?

sections.label: ComCare case numbers growth
sections.summary: ComCare cases grew, with Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance expanding about four times from 2007 to 2014.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The number of cases under ComCare has been growing, with that under ComCare Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance expanding about four times from 2007 to 2014.

sections.label: VWO funding and grant limits
sections.summary: Government increased VWO funding for staff pay and corporate capabilities, but most VWOs lack resources for proposals and grant restrictions limit usefulness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: In recent years, the Government has increased funding support for VWOs to make sure that VWOs are able to remunerate their staff better and granted funds to help improve the corporate capabilities of the social service sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: Most VWOs do not have resources to put up proposals to access the funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: Restrictions on grant usage limit the usefulness of some of such grants.

sections.label: Sustainable funding for VWOs
sections.summary: The speaker hopes Government will provide more sustainable recurrent funding or let VWOs explore creative revenue models.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: Moving forward, I hope that the Government will provide more sustainable and recurrent funding or allow VWOs to explore more creative revenue models to sustain their own operations.

sections.label: CDA First Step and KidSTART
sections.summary: MSF will give more financial support through CDA First Step and pilot KidSTART for vulnerable children aged six and below.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: MSF will also provide greater financial support to young children through the new CDA First Step scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: There is a small group of parents who, for various reasons, are unable to provide the best support to their children during this crucial stage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Hence, we will be piloting a new scheme targeted at vulnerable children aged six and below, called KidSTART.

sections.label: One-person household ComCare payout
sections.summary: From July this year, a one-person household will receive $500 per month, up from $450.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: From July this year, a one-person household will receive $500 per month, up from the current $450.

sections.label: Next Enabling Masterplan work
sections.summary: Work has started on the Enabling Masterplan for the next five years to better assist Persons with Disabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Much progress has been made under the current Enabling Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We will build on these efforts and have started work on the Enabling Masterplan for the next five years to explore how we can better assist Persons with Disabilities to integrate into mainstream society and live a meaningful life.

sections.label: ComChest Share as One matching
sections.summary: Over three years, the Government will provide dollar-for-dollar matching for additional donations raised through ComChest's Share as One programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Over the next three years, the Government will provide dollar-for-dollar matching for additional donations raised through ComChest's "Share as One" programme.

sections.label: Alimonies and aged parent maintenance
sections.summary: It cites alimonies for divorced men incapacitated during marriage and maintenance and care for aged parents, laws which must continue to evolve.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: For example, alimonies for divorced men who become incapacitated during marriage and cannot support themselves, or maintenance and care for aged parents; laws which will have to continue to evolve.

sections.label: Shaping environment, preventing problems
sections.summary: MSF wants to proactively shape the environment and prevent problems, conceiving its work as a strong start, a network for the vulnerable, and collective effort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We want to proactively and positively shape the environment and to prevent problems from developing where possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We conceive of our work in three ways − firstly, a strong start; secondly, a network for the vulnerable; and, lastly, a collective effort towards improving social welfare.

sections.label: Extra leg-up for less-advantaged children
sections.summary: Children who have less will get an extra leg-up, stronger safety nets will support the vulnerable, and assistance will be calibrated so those in greater need receive more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: For children who have less, we will give them an extra leg-up so that they, too, have the opportunity to live life to the fullest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We will build stronger safety nets to identify and support the more vulnerable in our society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We will calibrate our assistance so that those in greater need receive more.

sections.label: Empowering caring communities
sections.summary: One of MSF's priorities is to enable caring communities where individuals, businesses and VWOs work together so no Singaporean is left behind.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Page: 101 So, one of MSF's priorities is also to enable and empower caring communities where individuals, businesses and VWOs can come together, work together, to build a Singapore where everyone plays a role to make sure that no Singaporean is left behind.

sections.label: PREP marriage programme results
sections.summary: Since December 2014, MSF and community partners have offered PREP at the Registry of Marriage and community, with nine in 10 participants finding it helpful.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Since December 2014, MSF has worked with community partners to offer the Prevention and Relationship Enhancement Programme (PREP) at the Registry of Marriage and in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Nine in 10 participants told us the programme has been helpful in enhancing their marriage.

sections.label: Parenting programmes in schools
sections.summary: Parenting programmes aim to help parents, and outreach will expand from 50 schools to 175 schools by 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: They are meant to help parents become more competent in parenting, reduce parenting stress and to help them manage difficult behaviour in children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We have rolled out these programmes to 50 schools since 2014, benefiting 2,000 families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We will expand the outreach of these parenting programmes to 120 schools this year and up to 175 schools by 2018.

sections.label: Mothers on fathers caring
sections.summary: A 2016 MSF survey found close to three in four mothers agreed fathers are as good as them in caring for children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: A 2016 MSF survey of mothers with infants found that close to three in four mothers agreed that fathers are as good as them in caring for children.

sections.label: Childcare places target exceeded
sections.summary: Under the Childcare Master Plan, Singapore now has over 125,000 childcare places, an increase of over 30,000 in three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: In 2013, under our five-year Childcare Master Plan, we set a target to add 20,000 more childcare places, to have one place for every two children by 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Today, we have over 125,000 childcare places, an increase of over 30,000 places, compared to three years ago.

sections.label: New childcare centres and places
sections.summary: Five large childcare centres will add 2,000 places this year, and about 10,000 more places by 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Five large childcare centres will be completed this year, adding another 2,000 places in high demand estates like Punggol, Sengkang, Jurong West, Woodlands and Yishun.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Altogether, by 2017, about 10,000 more childcare places will be added in Singapore, of which about a third will be in Punggol and Sengkang.

sections.label: Childcare fees after subsidies
sections.summary: After subsidies, a median income family could pay about $350 monthly, and lower-income families as little as $3.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: After subsidies, a median income family could pay about $350 per month for childcare, while lower-income families who attend centres run by Anchor Operators could pay as little as $3 per month.

sections.label: Mandatory parenting programme for divorce
sections.summary: After the Women's Charter amendment, divorcing parents with minor children must attend a mandatory parenting programme before filing for divorce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: With the amendment of the Women's Charter in February this year, divorcing parents, with minor children, who are not able to agree on all matters of the divorce will have to attend a mandatory parenting programme before they can file for divorce.

sections.label: Singapore lower income child mobility
sections.summary: MOF's 2015 publication shows Singapore's lower income children have higher mobility than Denmark and almost twice the United States, with 14% reaching the top 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The most recent publication by MOF in 2015 shows that mobility for Singapore's lower income children is higher than in Denmark and almost twice as high as in the United States.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Among Singaporean children who start off with parents in the bottom 20th percentile, 14% of them end up in the top 20% of their peers.

sections.label: KidSTART support for vulnerable children
sections.summary: Existing efforts include immunisation, health checks, Development Support Programme and FLAiR, and a new KidSTART pilot will identify low-income children aged six and below for early support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: They include immunisation, health checks, Development Support Programme and the Focused Language Assistance in Reading (FLAiR), which supports language and literacy development in preschools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We will build on these existing efforts and pilot a new system of support called KidSTART.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: This new initiative will proactively identify low-income and vulnerable children aged six and below, to provide them with early access to health, learning and developmental support and monitor their progress during their early years.

sections.label: KidSTART pilot locations and reach
sections.summary: KidSTART will be piloted in Bukit Merah, Kreta Ayer, Boon Lay, Taman Jurong and Geylang Serai, reaching about 1,000 children in the first three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: For a start, we will pilot KidSTART in Bukit Merah, Kreta Ayer, Boon Lay, Taman Jurong and Geylang Serai.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We expect to reach out to about 1,000 children in the first three years.

sections.label: Unwed mothers and children benefits
sections.summary: Unwed mothers will benefit from Government-Paid Maternity Leave, and children of unwed parents will qualify for the CDA including the $3,000 CDA First Step.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Unwed mothers will benefit from Government-Paid Maternity Leave (GPML).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Children of unwed parents will qualify for the CDA, including the $3,000 CDA First Step.

sections.label: Families joining scheme
sections.summary: More than 100 families joined the scheme in the past two years, bringing the total to about 370 today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: More than 100 families have joined the scheme in the past two years, bringing the total number to about 370 today.

sections.label: Small-group homes and intervention
sections.summary: Smaller care ratios, training and therapeutic skills helped staff address behaviours and help children heal, and more small-group homes will be set up with strengthened intervention.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: But I also saw how smaller care ratios, training and therapeutic skills allowed the staff to better address these behaviours and to begin to help the children to heal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We will set up more small-group homes and strengthen the intervention to help these children.

sections.label: Safe and Strong Families pilot
sections.summary: A pilot called Safe and Strong Families will focus on improving parenting skills and family functioning so children remain safe in their families, with two main services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: With this in mind, we will be introducing a pilot called Safe and Strong Families and the focus is on improving the families' overall parenting skills and family functioning, so that the children can remain safe in their families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: This pilot will include two main services, namely, the Family Preservation Service and Family Reunification Service.

sections.label: Reaching 400 families
sections.summary: The aim is to reach out to 400 families and their vulnerable children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: For a start, we hope to reach out to 400 families and their vulnerable children.

sections.label: Supporting extended family ties
sections.summary: A long-term priority of the Ministry is to look into making it easier for extended families to support their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: While extended family ties still remain strong, one of my Ministry's long-term priorities will really be to look into how we can help make it even easier for extended families to support their loved ones.

sections.label: CDA First Step grant
sections.summary: MSF will administer the new CDA First Step, in which the Government deposits a $3,000 grant to the CDAs for newly born Singaporean children.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: As announced by the Minister for Finance, MSF will administer the new CDA First Step, in which the Government will deposit a $3,000 grant to the CDAs for newly born Singaporean children.

sections.label: KidSTART pilot for parents
sections.summary: A small group of parents needing more support will be helped by piloting a new system of support called KidSTART.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: There is a small group of parents who need more support in order to give their children a good start in life.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will enhance our support to them by piloting a new system of support called KidSTART.

sections.label: CDA and GPML for unwed parents
sections.summary: The benefits of the CDA, including the CDA First Step, will be extended to children of unwed parents, and unwed mothers may benefit from GPML.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We can do more to support their efforts to care for their children and reduce the disadvantages that their children may face at birth.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Hence, we have decided to extend the benefits of the CDA, including the CDA First Step, to children of unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We will also allow unwed mothers to benefit from GPML.

sections.label: ComCare financial assistance households
sections.summary: Households receiving ComCare short-to-medium term and long-term financial assistance rose from 24,000 in FY2012 to over 31,000 in 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The number of households who received ComCare short-to-medium term and long-term financial assistance increased from 24,000 in financial year 2012 to more than 31,000 in 2014.

sections.label: SSO officer safety measures
sections.summary: CCTV and duress alarms are installed at all SSO interview rooms, and SSO and selected frontline officers are trained in de-escalation and self-defence.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: While they have a good working relationship with most of those who seek help, they do encounter a few who may be verbally or physically abusive.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We have installed CCTV and duress alarms at all SSO interview rooms.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: We are training SSO and selected frontline officers in de-escalation and self-defence.

sections.label: System rollout at SSOs and FSCs
sections.summary: The system launched early this year has been rolled out at all 24 SSOs and 46 FSCs.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Since we launched the system early this year, it has been rolled out at all 24 SSOs and 46 FSCs.

sections.label: Cash assistance rate increase
sections.summary: From this July, cash assistance for one-person households rises from $450 to $500, with rates also increasing for larger households.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Starting this July, we will increase the cash assistance rate for one-person households from $450 to $500.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: The rates will also increase for larger households.

sections.label: New Vulnerable Adults Act
sections.summary: The Ministry will enact a new Vulnerable Adults Act later this year to intervene earlier to protect vulnerable adults from harm.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This could result in them having to fend for themselves or being abused by their caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: So, later this year, my Ministry will enact a new Vulnerable Adults Act.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: This will allow us to intervene earlier to protect them from harm.

sections.label: Case resolution through conciliation
sections.summary: More than 80% of cases were resolved through conciliation, and of the remainder, four in 10 settled out of court after further mediation.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Since then, more than 80% of cases have been resolved through conciliation.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Of the remainder, four in 10 were successfully settled out of court after further mediation.

sections.label: Youth programme pilot
sections.summary: MSF will work with two appointed social service agencies to pilot youth programmes later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
sentences.text: Later this year, MSF will work with two appointed social service agencies to pilot a suite of youth programmes.

sections.label: Employment credits and Workfare support
sections.summary: Special Employment Credits, Workfare Income Supplement and Workfare Training Support Scheme support persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Between 2012 and 2015, $44 million of Special Page: 114 Employment Credits were given to employers who hired 9,200 eligible persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Over the same period, the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme supplemented the income of more than 7,400 low-wage persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: From 1 January 2017, persons with disabilities aged below 35 will also be able to tap on the Workfare Training Support Scheme to improve their skills.

sections.label: Job placements for persons with disabilities
sections.summary: SG Enable and partners placed more than 750 persons with disabilities into employment over the past two years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In 2015, over 500 job vacancies were posted and more than 200 persons with disabilities registered in the portal.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Overall, SG Enable and its partners – Autism Resource Centre, Movement for the Intellectually Disabled of Singapore and SPD – have collectively placed more than 750 persons with disabilities into employment over the past two years.

sections.label: Steering Committee study areas
sections.summary: The Committee will study areas including early intervention, education, employment, service delivery, families, transitions and inclusive community.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Committee will be studying a wide range of areas, including: first, enabling persons with disabilities to reach their potential through further efforts in early intervention, education, employment, lifelong learning and health; second, improving service delivery and quality by harnessing data and organising services; third, supporting their families and caregivers; fourth, smoothening transitions across different services at different life stages; and, fifth, fostering an accessible and inclusive community through public education, technology, disabled-friendly spaces, as well as sports and community integration.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Committee will examine where and how we can "mainstream" the support given to persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Just like what we have done with the public transport system, we should see how key national infrastructure and initiatives, including SkillsFuture and Smart Nation, can be just as relevant to persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Indeed, we will encourage the Committee to dream big, dive deep and dare to deal with the difficult.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: I, therefore, assure Mr Seah, Ms Phua and Ms Chia that the Steering Committee will look into the issues that they have raised today.

sections.label: Caregivers over-protective of loved ones
sections.summary: Caregivers shared they are sometimes over-protective because the public cannot empathise with challenges faced.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Caregivers have shared with me that they are sometimes over-protective of their loved ones with disabilities because the larger public is unable to empathise with the challenges they face.

sections.label: Funding for social service sector
sections.summary: Matching grants and $350 million into the Tote Board Social Service Fund will support over 300 programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In addition to the VWO-Charities Capability Fund, the Government and Tote Board have set aside half a billion dollars in matching grants under the Care & Share movement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: ComChest and VWOs can draw on this half a billion dollars to build better capabilities and better prepare themselves for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In addition, MSF has also secured the Tote Board's support for an injection of $350 million into the Tote Board Social Service Fund over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This funding will support more than 300 programmes, including essential flagship programmes that benefit families, children and persons with disabilities.

sections.label: NCSS HR consultancy programme
sections.summary: NCSS will soon launch a three-year HR consultancy programme supporting up to 100 VWOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: NCSS will soon launch a three-year HR consultancy programme that will support up to 100 VWOs.

sections.label: SkillsFuture priority sectors
sections.summary: The Social Service and Early Childhood sectors will be priority sectors under SkillsFuture, with Sectoral Manpower Plans developed in the coming year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The Social Service and the Early Childhood sectors will be priority sectors under SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We will be developing SkillsFuture Sectoral Manpower Plans for both sectors in the coming year.

sections.label: Two tripartite committees set up
sections.summary: Two separate tripartite committees have been set up, one for the social service sector and another for the early childhood sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: To spearhead this effort, we have set up two separate tripartite committees – one for the social service sector and another for the early childhood sector.

sections.label: Matching additional SHARE donations
sections.summary: The Government will match additional SHARE donations from 1 April 2016, dollar-for-dollar above financial year 2015 levels until end March 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We want to encourage more Singaporeans like Mr Tan, and more employers like those Mr Tan works for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: So, the Government will match additional donations made through SHARE from 1 April 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Donations above levels in financial year 2015 will be matched dollar-for-dollar for the next three years, until end March 2019.

sections.label: Resources to protect vulnerable groups
sections.summary: The sum of resources, time, skills and energy must count enough to ensure vulnerable groups are taken care of and no Singaporean is left behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The sum of our resources, time, skills and energy, that sum must count enough to make sure that vulnerable groups are taken care of, that no Singaporean is left behind.

sections.label: Purple Parade participant growth
sections.summary: The Purple Parade, supported by Ms Denise Phua and worked on with the Central Singapore CDC, VWOs and Manpower Groups Singapore, grew from 4,500 participants in 2013 to 6,000 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: One very clear example is the Purple Parade, and Ms Denise Phua is a very strong supporter.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We work with the Central Singapore CDC, VWOs, Manpower Groups Singapore and so on, and the number of participants has increased from 4,500 in 2013 to 6,000 in 2015.

sections.label: Assistance for single unwed mothers
sections.summary: The Minister is heartened that assistance will be extended to vulnerable single unwed mothers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: Minister, I am heartened to know that assistance will be extended to vulnerable single unwed mothers.

sections.label: Changes for single unwed moms
sections.summary: Changes for single unwed moms apply to all regardless of vulnerability, and SNTC looks beyond financial trust to accommodation and social requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, for the areas of change for single unwed moms, it applies to all single unwed moms, regardless of their degree of vulnerability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For the second one, with regard to the Special Needs Trust Company Limited (SNTC), beyond the trust relating to the financial aspect, we also look at other aspects in terms of accommodation and in terms of some of the social requirements.

sections.label: Non-responding families and child protection
sections.summary: Where families do not respond, the question is whether this falls into neglect and whether Child Protection needs to be activated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In cases where families do not respond, this is where we also need to take a look at whether it falls into the realms of neglect for the child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: If the family is in a particularly vulnerable situation, children are not going to school for a host of reasons when they should be, and we are working with the parents and they are not responding, would this be a situation where Child Protection needs to be activated and it needs to come in?

sections.label: Further measures for non-cooperation
sections.summary: Where families still choose not to work with them, they will see whether children are neglected and further measures are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Where they still choose not to work with us, then we will have to see whether the children are being neglected and further measures need to be taken.

sections.label: No clear definition of graduation
sections.summary: There is no clear definition of graduation because of the different complexities and needs of families on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: You realise that there are people, even though you have helped, who seem to be able to do better now, but they still need help, because they need the support not only for themselves but also for their families.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: That is why in my answer earlier, I shared that there is no clear definition of graduation because, on the ground, we see the different complexities, the different needs of families.

sections.label: Flexibility on age criterion
sections.summary: The member asks whether the Minister will consider flexibility on the age criterion for existing cases beyond six years of age.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Intervening for disadvantaged children is crucial and the earlier the assistance is given, the better it is.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo
sentences.text: Thus, may I ask the Minister whether he will consider flexibility on the age criterion for existing cases on a case-by-case basis beyond the six years of age?

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Chairman, right now, we are looking at those aged six and below.

sections.label: SSO upfront deployment
sections.summary: The SSO set-up aims to forward-deploy SSOs upfront, especially for complex cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Perhaps, to reinforce the response given earlier to Assoc Prof Daniel Goh, the whole idea with the set-up of the SSO is to forward-deploy a lot of our SSOs upfront, especially to deal with complex cases.

sections.label: Tribunal option and SSO help
sections.summary: The position is that cases should be shared so the SSO can help, with the Tribunal also considered.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As I have mentioned in my answer earlier, we also look at the option via the Tribunal.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Our position is this: every case that you come across as such, we would like you to share with us and see how the SSO can help in the process.

sections.label: ECDA works with agencies
sections.summary: ECDA will work with other Government agencies to help fellow Singaporeans, like the SSOs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Like the SSOs, ECDA will also work with other Government agencies to see how we can help fellow Singaporeans.
